header:
Date: 2025-05-20
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Michael Chen (Redwood AE), Sara Patel (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood Security PM), Dr. Anita Rao (CISO, SummitCare), Marcus Lee (Head of Eng), Priya Desai (Compliance)
summary: Posture review focused on SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 evidence access, RBAC/SSO integrations, audit logs and SIEM ingestion, data residency for EU patients, and customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM). Action: Redwood to share reports and Trust Center access; SE to map controls to SummitCare matrix.
topics: SOC 2 Type II report availability; ISO 27001 certificate and scope; Trust Center access and evidence bundles; RBAC and SSO (Okta/SCIM) integration; audit logs export and retention; KMS/customer-managed keys and HSM support; data residency (EU and US); private deployment options and controls mapping.
transcript:
[00:00] Michael Chen: Hi everyone thanks for joining, uh we scheduled 45 minutes for a posture review focused on SOC 2 / ISO. Could do quick intros, then we can jump into specific controls you wanted to map.
[00:09] Dr. Anita Rao: Hi all, Anita here, CISO. Thanks Michael. We want to validate the scope of your SOC 2, understand evidence access, and confirm how keys and logs are handled for PHI.
[00:20] Marcus Lee: Marcus, head of eng. We're most concerned about audit logs, retention, and SSO provisioning.
[00:27] Michael Chen: Great. Sara, Liam — do you want to do a quick runbook on what's in the Trust Center and what we can share?
[00:33] Sara Patel: Yep. Hi, Sara SE. So Redwood maintains a Trust Center with SOC 2 Type II report, ISO 27001 certificate, plus evidence bundles for a number of controls. We can invite your team to read-only access; the invite goes to an email domain or specific accounts. Note: some evidence is redacted for third-party items.
[00:52] Priya Desai: Does the Trust Center include the controls mapping to NIST or ISO clauses? We have an internal matrix — mapping is easiest for us.
[01:01] Liam O'Connor: Yes we have an internal controls mapping sheet we can share — it shows which Redwood controls map to SOC 2 CC/ISO 27001 clauses and where evidence lives. I will attach the mapping as a spreadsheet after the call.
[01:14] Dr. Anita Rao: Ok good. On KMS — we need to know if customer-managed keys are supported, hardened HSMs, and whether keys can be region-locked for EU residency.
[01:26] Sara Patel: Short answer: we support customer-managed keys via a KMS integration and we have an HSM-backed option for Dedicated or Private deployments. For hosted, we support AWS KMS customer key policy — you can bring your own CMK for data-at-rest encryption. Region locking depends on the provider region; for fully private on-prem we can accommodate strict region constraints.
[01:48] Marcus Lee: Is that available for embeddings / vector stores as well or just model weights and S3 objects?
[01:54] Sara Patel: We encrypt all persisted artifacts — embeddings, cached KV stores, and model shards — with the same envelope encryption. The object storage buckets are encrypted using your CMK when configured.
[02:05] Michael Chen: I'm going to share a link to the Trust Center in the chat — please note some docs are access-controlled and flagged as 'redacted' where needed.
[02:12] [link shared: https://trust.redwood.ai/org/summitcare-invite]
[02:17] Priya Desai: Great. About audit logs — we need an ingestion path into our SIEM (Sumo/QRadar). How do you surface logs?
[02:26] Sara Patel: We stream audit logs to customers via secure syslog or CloudTrail integration, and we also offer S3 delivery of audit bundles. Logs include admin actions, token creation, role assignment, and API call traces. There is an event schema we can share.
[02:42] Marcus Lee: Sampling question — are system-level logs and application-level logs both available?
[02:47] Liam O'Connor: Yes, we surface both. System logs (infrastructure) are available for Dedicated/Private; for hosted, we provide operational audit logs and API-level traces. For deeper infra logs we'd recommend Dedicated or Private where you get more control and optional VPC peering.
[03:07] Dr. Anita Rao: What about retention? We need 7 years for some records for our regulator.
[03:13] Sara Patel: By default hosted audit log retention is 365 days in the Trust Center export; we can provide longer retention as an add-on or via S3 delivery where you control lifecycle policies. For Dedicated/Private, retention is configurable.
[03:26] Priya Desai: Can we get a runbook on what is included in the SOC 2 Type II — which controls were in scope specifically?
[03:34] Michael Chen: Yes, the SOC 2 report includes scope and the period — we'll send the Type II report PDF and the controls listing. Some evidence attachments are available in the Trust Center.
[03:43] [03:43] Michael Chen: Quick aside, il — sorry — quick note: some vendor names in the report are abbreviated by the auditor, so there may be small mismatches.
[03:51] Priya Desai: Good to know, transcription and doc naming can be messy.
[03:55] Marcus Lee: On SSO and provisioning — we use Okta and want SCIM for user provisioning. How granular is your RBAC model?
[04:04] Sara Patel: We support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning with Okta. RBAC is role-based with admin/editor/viewer plus custom roles in Dedicated/Private. We also integrate with your org's groups for access control. SCIM supports group sync for large teams.
[04:22] Dr. Anita Rao: Do you support JIT join and SSO enforced MFA? We require enforced MFA for all admin access.
[04:28] Liam O'Connor: We enforce SSO MFA policies when SSO is enabled; admin roles require MFA. For additional controls we support device checks via conditional access if your IdP supports it.
[04:40] Priya Desai: For auditability we need immutable event IDs and a proof chain. Does the audit log include request IDs that tie to token issuance and KV cache ops?
[04:50] Sara Patel: Yes, each API call has a request ID and correlation ID; token lifecycle events are logged as well. KV cache hits/misses are logged in a summarized form to avoid huge volumes, but we can surface more detail for a specific pilot workload.
[05:06] Marcus Lee: On encryption in transit — TLS versions, cipher suites? We're on a high baseline.
[05:11] Liam O'Connor: TLS 1.2 and 1.3 supported, we prefer 1.3 for new sessions. We can provide cipher suite list. Mutual TLS is available for Dedicated/Private for service-to-service.
[05:24] Dr. Anita Rao: ISO 27001 — can you confirm certificate scope and whether PHI handling was in scope?
[05:31] Michael Chen: The ISO 27001 cert scope covers the hosted API and the Redwood control plane; PHI-specific handling is not automatically covered unless there's a dedicated contract and controls for healthcare data. We'll call out scope in the certificate we share.
[05:45] Priya Desai: Do you have attestation or policies for business continuity and backups? Our auditors will ask about RTO/RPO.
[05:53] Sara Patel: Yes, we have documented BCP and DR policies; for Dedicated we provide SLA parameters including RTO/RPO targets. Those docs are linked in the Trust Center under continuity and incident response.
[06:06] Marcus Lee: If we needed a private deployment (on-prem or VPC), what is the onboarding time and the security review cadence?
[06:14] Liam O'Connor: Typical private deployment onboarding is 8-12 weeks depending on environment and compliance gating; security reviews are quarterly for Dedicated and as agreed for Private, with evidence packages provided.
[06:27] Michael Chen: For the controls mapping step — Sara will produce a spreadsheet mapping Redwood control IDs to SOC 2 criteria and ISO clauses and we can align that to SummitCare's control matrix.
[06:35] Sara Patel: I'll add notes where evidence is only available for Dedicated/Private or where redaction applies.
[06:41] Priya Desai: Regarding data residency, our EU footprint requires patient data at rest to reside in the EU. How do you support region isolation for hosted?
[06:52] Sara Patel: For hosted, we can pin workloads to EU regions depending on account and plan; we also offer Private deployment in EU regions. For stricter residency we recommend Dedicated capacity or Private where storage and keys remain in the specified region.
[07:07] Marcus Lee: Any network controls for egress restrictions? We want to block outbound calls except to allowed endpoints.
[07:13] Liam O'Connor: Egress controls are part of the Private/Dedicated offering — you can restrict outbound network flows, and for hosted we provide VPC peering options with controlled egress.
[07:26] Dr. Anita Rao: About penetration tests and vulnerabilities — do you publish results or a summary?
[07:33] Michael Chen: We run annual third-party pen tests and will provide an executive summary and remediation status. Full reports are sensitive and provided under NDA where applicable.
[07:44] Priya Desai: We will likely need a copy of the executive summary and vuln remediation SLAs.
[07:49] Michael Chen: Noted — we'll include that in the attachment pack.
[07:54] Marcus Lee: For the controls mapping I also want to validate operational evidence for patching, endpoint management, and supply chain vendor assessments.
[08:04] Sara Patel: Those map to change management and vendor risk controls — evidence includes vulnerability scans, vendor contracts, and patch schedules, which we can reference.
[08:14] Dr. Anita Rao: One more point — log integrity. We want to feed logs into our WORM storage for long-term retention. Is that feasible?
[08:22] Liam O'Connor: Yes — via S3 delivery to your bucket with tight lifecycle and WORM policies you control. We'll provide signed manifests for ingestion verification.
[08:31] Priya Desai: About identity lifecycle — does Redwood support deprovisioning automation and SCIM group-to-role mapping? We have frequent contractor rotations.
[08:41] Sara Patel: SCIM supports group-to-role mapping and you can set deprovisioning windows. We can also support webhook notifications for user state changes to drive further automation.
[08:54] Marcus Lee: For encryption keys — if we rotate keys, what's the impact window? Can you re-encrypt objects in place or do we need a migration?
[09:02] Sara Patel: We use envelope encryption; key rotation is supported and re-encryption is handled transparently for new objects. For existing persisted blobs we can schedule background re-encryption; the timeline depends on dataset size.
[09:16] Dr. Anita Rao: Ok thanks. On legal side — we may need a BAA for PHI and clauses for subprocessor lists. Can you share your subprocessor list?
[09:26] Michael Chen: Subprocessor list is in the Trust Center; we keep it updated and can provide a CSV. For BAAs we have standard language and will engage legal once we have scoping.
[09:36] Priya Desai: Will you include redlined security addendum templates? That helps accelerate legal review.
[09:41] Michael Chen: We can share standard addenda; any redlines can be discussed with our legal ops.
[09:47] [09:47] Michael Chen: Quick recap before we close — we'll share: SOC 2 Type II report, ISO 27001 certificate, Trust Center invite, controls mapping spreadsheet, executive summary of pen test, and the subprocessor list. Sara will do initial mapping to your control matrix.
[10:03] Dr. Anita Rao: That sounds good. Priya and Marcus are the owners on our side for the mapping and technical follow-ups.
[10:11] Priya Desai: Yes, I'll send the control matrix and any regulator-specific notes.
[10:16] Marcus Lee: We'll likely run a short pilot with a subset of workloads to validate logs and encryption behavior.
[10:22] Michael Chen: Great, I'll get those artifacts into the Trust Center and message the invite. Shall we schedule the follow-up for two weeks?
[10:29] Dr. Anita Rao: Two weeks works.
[10:32] Michael Chen: Perfect — thanks everyone. Action items noted in chat.
[10:36] [END OF RECORDING]

Meeting notes appended to transcript: Next steps and action items in chat; Trust Center link shared. Some parts of the transcript may have minor transcription errors (proper nouns abbreviated).
